description: One corridor folded into three stacked runs joined at alternating ends: a plain walk east on the bottom floor, a 20px-high no-jumping channel walked back west on the middle floor, and a hop east along one-way shelves on the top floor before a two-ledge chain up to the ceiling door. The twist is that the right third of the room has no middle floor at all, so the top run's shelves hang over a two-storey void and a missed hop does not kill you, it demotes you to the bottom run and you walk the whole spine again.

Nothing is intentionally gated - wall/dash only make it faster (west-ceiling 223/139).

Route shape (ascent, west to ceiling): walk east on the bottom floor to the block at cols 18-20 (20px step up), 30px hop up-left onto the middle floor at col 16, walk west along the 20px channel (rows 10-11, ceiling row 9 at cols 5-8 and 11-14), emerge at col 4 where the ceiling is open, 20px hop onto the left step (cols 0-3, rows 10-11), 10px step onto the top run at col 5, 20px hop across the hole at cols 9-10, then ledge row 6 cols 9-10 and ledge row 3 cols 12-14 up and out. Descent (ceiling to west) is the fall: drop into the right-hand void and walk out left.

Coins: coin 0 (250,140) bottom run, in the drop zone east of the fold stair - easy, worst shaky 32/32 from ceiling (11/32 from west, so treat ceiling as its home door). coin 1 (80,102) mid-channel - worst shaky 27/32 from ceiling, 16/32 (50%) from west. coin 2 (292,78) is the hard bonus on the far one-way shelf, three hops out over the void: solved from ceiling at `none` (104 ticks, 32/32) and from west with wall/dash; a miss costs the whole spine.

Hazard cadence matters for integration: the single shutter is `hazard 120 100 10 20 56 16 0` (on 16 ticks in 56, slowed from 40/12 after playtest reaction-time feedback). Longer periods are NOT safe - period 60, 90 or 150 makes west-ceiling inconclusive at `none` purely by blowing up the solver's state space, not by geometry (56 solves at 507 ticks of the ~600 horizon). Keep the period at 56 or shorter if this hazard is retuned.

Two physics constraints future edits must respect: (a) the 20px channel gives no jump headroom, so the middle floor's right entry (cols 15-16) and the column before the left step (col 4) must stay free of row-9 ceiling; (b) the solver's path horizon is ~600 ticks, and this route already uses 371, so lengthening any run or adding a climb step will make the no-ability ascent go inconclusive.

description: One corridor folded three times: a low 2-tile tunnel east along rows 15-16, a two-step stair at the east wall up into a middle floor that doubles back west under a 20px ceiling, a second fold at the west wall onto a top run that hops east over one-way platforms and two open holes to the ceiling shaft at cols 14-17. The twist is that the two holes (cols 8-10 and 20-22) are cut clean through rows 6-14, so a missed hop does not kill you, it demotes you two floors and makes you re-run the whole spine — and because there is one coin on each run, the room has to be run cleanly once rather than sloppily three times.
notes: Doors: west (bottom tunnel) and ceiling (shaft cols 14-17). Pair results from the final `--shaky` run: at dash all four pairs solve (west->ceiling 136, ceiling->west 89, west->west 5, ceiling->ceiling 12); at wall all four solve (west->ceiling 453); at none, ceiling->west, west->west and ceiling->ceiling solve, and west->ceiling is inconclusive. IMPORTANT CAVEAT for the assembler: that inconclusive is a solver-budget artifact, not geometry. The auditor caps the search at a fixed node budget (every failure reports exactly 14550 expanded / 127670 generated nodes, deepest_path_ticks 600); probing intermediate targets shows the ability-free fold route is reachable at `none` all the way to the west end of the middle run (coin 1 solves from west at none in 349 ticks), and only the last fold + top run + shaft fall outside the budget. So the ability-free three-run spine is built and intended; I have declared the minimum loadout as `dash` because that is what the solver can actually prove end-to-end. Treat `ability_requirement: dash` as the verified figure and the ability-free spine as designed-but-unproven. Deliberate ability gating that IS geometrically obvious: the two chutes climb 60px (bottom floor y=170 to middle floor y=110) and 50px (middle y=110 to top y=60), both past the 40px jump, so with dash or a wall-jump chain the player can climb a chute and skip the folds entirely — that is exactly the shortcut the dash solve takes (136 ticks vs 453 for the wall route that uses more of the spine). Hazard cadence: one shutter, `hazard 150 90 10 20 90 15 0` — col 15 across the full 20px height of the crawl (cols 14-18), 90-tick period, 15 ticks hot, phase 0. The crawl has no headroom to jump the shutter, so it must be walked on timing; that is what makes the middle run's demotion a timing loss rather than a free retry. One-way platforms are at row 3 cols 14-15 (shaft rung) and row 6 cols 11-13 (optional deliberate drop-through into the middle run); all have the required 2 empty tiles above. Boundary is intact: the only gaps are col 0 rows 13-16 and row 0 cols 14-17.

description: Four one-way strata at rows 4/7/10/13, each holed in two columns, stack the room into a drop-through sorting puzzle: you fall in through the ceiling, land on the top stratum between its two holes, and pick a lane layer by layer. The twist is that both lanes reach both exits, so the choice is pure risk/reward - a near-aligned left lane is a spike-fringed freefall to the bottom-left chamber, while the braided right lane costs a walk on every stratum but is spike-free and carries both easy coins.

COINS: coin 0 (140,110) EASY, inside the island pocket, solved from all three doors at none; worst shaky 26/32 west, 28/32 floor, 16/32 (=50%) ceiling. coin 1 (290,40) BONUS, top-run ledge across the descent shaft mouth: solved from ceiling at none (worst shaky 29/32), inconclusive from west/floor at none. coin 2 (50,25) BONUS, mid-air high in the left ascent shaft: solved from ceiling at none (18/32) and from every door with wall (up to 31/32).
HAZARD: one shutter, hazard 240 90 40 20 150 40 0, in the gap between the two descent catches. Note for the assembler: the mere presence of a timed hazard roughly halves the solver's effective search budget — ceiling-floor at none only became solvable after the chimney was moved next to the ceiling-door landing block. Do not move the chimney (cols 18-19) or the row-16 launcher block (cols 18-21) without re-auditing.

description: Three wide, tall chambers separated by two full-height partitions whose only opening is a floor-level 3-tile doorway filled by a timed shutter; each chamber has an unbroken floor, so each is a bank point and progress is "read the beat, walk through" with no jump or spike involved. The twist is that the two shutters run in exact antiphase (period 180, shut 60, phases 120 and 30), so one gate closing announces the other opening — and both entrances are phased to get a free first gate, while a coin sitting inside gate 2's mouth turns a doorway into the thing you have to time, and a sealed dash-crawl vent lane above the chambers offers an untimed express route that can never bank.
notes:
GRID: partitions at cols 10 and 21, solid rows 3-13 with a 1-tile dash-crawl vent at row 4 and the gate mouth open at rows 14-16. Lane floor is solid row 5 with access holes at cols 7-9 and 22-24; three-rung one-way ladders (rows 8/11/14) in chambers 1 and 3 sit against the partitions, deliberately away from the door mouths (moving them out of the entry path was what fixed early DropRepeatFrame fragility). Floor row 17 unbroken; rock rows 0-2.

LOADOUTS: door-to-door and both easy coins need NO abilities. west-west, west-east, east-west, east-east all solved at none (5/163/180/6 ticks). The overhead lane is gated by the 1-tile (10px) vents against a 12px standing player — geometrically obvious dash-only, and 40px of jump cannot open it. Climbing to the lane needs no abilities, so a player up there can always come back down; only CROSSING it needs dash. No wall-gated pairs.

COINS: coin 0 (152,158) mid-chamber-2 floor and coin 1 (212,158) inside gate 2's mouth are the easy pair — at loadout none, worst shaky is 32/32 from west and 30/32 from east for both, i.e. 94-100%. Coin 2 (152,38) is the hard bonus on the sealed stretch of overhead lane above chamber 2: solved at dash from west (shaky 16/32) and at both from east (31/41); inconclusive at none/wall as intended.

CAVEAT for the assembler: at the WALL loadout the solver picks a riskier east-side line and coin 0 drops to 15/32. That is the solver spending a tool it does not need, not a route the room asks for — the intended and only necessary loadout is none, where all easy numbers are >=94%.

HAZARD CADENCE: both gates period 180 / active 60. Gate 1 (x100,y140,10x30) phase 120; gate 2 (x210,y140,10x30) phase 30. Offset is exactly 90 = half period, so the gates are never shut together; there are two 30-tick windows per cycle with both open, which is the "ride the wave" sprint line. Do not re-phase these to 0/90 — that leaves the near gate shut at spawn and drops west-side robustness to ~50%.

description: Four chambers in a west-east chain, separated by three full-height partitions each pierced by one shuttered doorway; every chamber has a clear floor at row 16 so it is a bank point, and progress means being in the right chamber on the right beat. The twist is a travelling wave rather than strict alternation — the three gates open west-to-east with a 40-tick lag, so heading east you can sprint through all three in one cycle while retreating west runs against the wave and forces a chamber-at-a-time shuffle, and the three gates are physically different (3-tile run-through, 2-tile squeeze, elevated causeway) so no gate is crossed the same way twice.
notes: Doors west+east; minimum loadout for every ordered pair including both self-pairs is NONE (all gates are walks or 20px steps, all ladder rungs are 20px rises) — nothing in the room is ability-gated, so there are no gated pairs to keep inconclusive. Final --shaky run: west->east none solved 261, east->west none solved 213, west->west 5, east->east 6. Coin difficulty: coin 0 (100,160, C2 floor) easy, worst shaky 32/32 from west at none; coin 1 (150,160) sits INSIDE the gate-B hazard footprint — grab-and-retreat, 24/32 from west at none; coin 2 (290,60, east tower on the row-7 stub at cols 29-30) is the hard bonus, solved from east at none (6/32) and 35/57 from west with dash, 64/81 from east with wall. Hazard cadence: all three shutters period 120, active (closed) 48, open 72; phases 0 / 40 / 80 at cols 8 / 15 / 22, i.e. a +40-tick travelling wave. Gate A is x80 y140 10x30, gate B x150 y150 10x20, gate C x220 y130 10x20. Structural notes for the assembler: rows 0-4 are solid ceiling (no dead space); the overhead bypass is a 2-tile tunnel at rows 5-6 that crosses partitions 8 and 22 but NOT partition 15, which runs solid to the ceiling — so the bypass is two disjoint galleries and gate B can never be skipped. Ladders are staggered one-way rungs at rows 13/11/9 in each chamber with 2 empty tiles above every rung. Gate C's passage is an elevated causeway: solid blocks at cols 20-21 and 23-24 rows 15-16 with the col-22 aperture at rows 13-14.

description: Five floor-bearing chambers separated by four shutter gates whose phases march eastward as a travelling wave (72/48/24/0, period 120, active 66), so an eastbound player can ride one continuous sprint through every gate while a westbound player meets the wave head-on and must bank a full cycle in each chamber. The twist is the middle partition: a true airlock with two valves half a period apart -- an upper lane over a solid slab and a lower lane at floor level -- never open together, so crossing the room's centre means picking a lane on the beat and paying a 30px climb if you pick wrong.
notes: Grid: partitions cols 6/12/18/24; gates are 20px floor-level run-throughs at rows 15-16 (no spikes, no gaps, danger is 100% temporal). Airlock at col 18 has slab at row 14, upper valve rows 12-13 (phase 24) and lower valve rows 15-16 (phase 84); step blocks at (16,16)/(20,16) and ledges at (17,14)/(19,14) are the only lane-change, two 20px hops. Hazard cadence: period 120, active 66 (shut more than open), 54-tick window, opening rolls east one gate every 24 ticks. Both intended pairs (west<->east) and both self-pairs solve at loadout none; wall/dash add nothing structurally, they only shave ticks. Coins: coin 0 (90,160) EASY, chamber B, worst shaky 32/32 from west; coin 1 (180,130) HARD BONUS sitting inside the upper valve's own footprint on the slab (grab-and-retreat), 7/32 from west, 9/32 from east -- comfortably >=1 success; coin 2 (270,160) chamber E past all four gates, 19/32 (59%) from east, inconclusive from west at none because the full west-to-east coin route exceeds the solver's 600-tick path horizon, not because it is gated. Nothing in the room is a spike hop or a chimney.
